summary: Obfuscated preinstall hook fetches Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The npm package declares a `preinstall` hook that runs `setup.mjs`, itself heavily obfuscated with `_0xNNNN` identifiers and per-function proxy objects mediating calls to `execFileSync`, `https.get`, unzip, and `chmod`. On install, `setup.mjs` checks for `bun` on PATH and, if absent, downloads a Bun runtime archive from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`, extracts `bun`/`bun.exe` into a tempdir, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling `math_init.js` — a 720 KB single-line, control-flow-flattened, string-array-rotated bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` whose contents cannot be read by standard Node-based tooling. The package advertises itself as a key-value-storage SDK, which does not require fetching a second language runtime to execute an opaque bundle at install time. This pattern — fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute a bundled obfuscated payload during `npm install` — grants arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine while bypassing Node-based static analysis, and the payload's actual behavior is not observable without running it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
